Spherical linear interpolation of rotations

Source: R/quaternions.R
quaternion_slerp.Rd

Interpolates between two orientations along the shortest great circle: \(q(s) = q_1 (q_1^{*} q_2)^s\) for \(s \in [0, 1]\). The sign of \(q_2\) is flipped when needed so the path is the shorter of the two arcs that represent the same pair of rotations. For nearly identical inputs the method falls back to normalized linear interpolation.

quaternion_slerp(q1, q2, s)

Arguments

q1, q2

Start and end orientations: quaternions, rotation matrices or robot_rotation objects.

s

Interpolation parameter(s) in \([0, 1]\).

Value

A robot_quaternion when s is a scalar, otherwise a list.

Examples

qa <- robot_quaternion(c(1, 0, 0, 0))
qb <- robot_quaternion(robot_rotation(axis = c(0, 0, 1), angle = pi / 2))
quaternion_slerp(qa, qb, 0.5)
#> <robot_quaternion> w = 0.92388, (x, y, z) = (0, 0, 0.382683)
